# `Browser.Geolocation.Internals`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Browser.Geolocation.Internals — the full, low-level geolocation port
surface: the closed outbound/inbound ADTs, the complete `Options` knob set, and
the raw `Ipe.Ffi.Js` request/subscribe wiring the high-level `Ipe.Browser.Geolocation`
layer wraps with sane defaults.

A caller that needs every option (accuracy, timeout, cache age) reaches for this
module directly; everyone else uses the high-level layer. Both disclose
`js-port:geolocation` — the disclosure is keyed on the canonical
`Ipe.Browser.<Api>` path prefix, so importing either the module or its
`Internals` submodule discloses the same web axis.

## `Options`

The `getCurrentPosition` / `watchPosition` option knobs, mirroring the Web API
`PositionOptions`:

  * `enableHighAccuracy` — request the best-available accuracy (may be slower /
    costlier); `False` accepts a coarse fix.
  * `timeout` — the maximum time to wait for a fix, in milliseconds. A value ≤ 0
    means "no deadline".
  * `maximumAge` — accept a cached fix up to this many milliseconds old; 0
    forces a fresh fix.

## `defaults`

```ipe
defaults : Options
```

Sane defaults: a coarse fix, no deadline, always fresh — the values the
high-level `current` / `watch` use.

## `JsCmd`

The ONE closed OUTBOUND port type: the whole outbound surface as a single
auditable object. `Current`/`Watch` carry the full option record; `ClearWatch`
ends an active watch.

## `JsMsg`

The NARROW closed INBOUND port type — deliberately NOT the app's internal
`Msg`. Every variant the browser can push is enumerated, so the fold in the
high-level layer is EXHAUSTIVE and a permission denial can never be silently
dropped: it becomes a typed `Err`.

  * `Position lat lng accuracy` — a fix (degrees, degrees, metres).
  * `Denied` — the host refused the location permission.
  * `Unavailable` — the position could not be determined.
  * `Timeout` — no fix arrived within the requested deadline.

## `request`

```ipe
request : JsCmd -> Cmd.Cmd msg
```

`request cmd` — hand a closed outbound `JsCmd` to the raw port transport.
The served first-party JS sink reaches `navigator.geolocation.*`; the reply
arrives inbound as a `JsMsg`.

## `requestOne`

```ipe
requestOne : JsCmd -> Task Error JsMsg
```

`requestOne cmd` — correlated one-shot `JsCmd` → `Task Error JsMsg`.
Routes through `Js.request` with the `inbound` decoder so the correlated
reply is decoded fail-closed by the same gate the `subscribe` path uses.

## `subscribe`

```ipe
subscribe : (JsMsg -> msg) -> Sub.Sub msg
```

`subscribe toMsg` — the inbound subscription over the fail-closed seal
decoder. `inbound` IS the security gate; a malformed / mismatched frame is
dropped whole. A decoded `JsMsg` is handed to `toMsg`.

## `inbound`

```ipe
inbound : Decode.Decoder JsMsg
```

The total, fail-closed decoder for a `JsMsg` frame of this capability.

It first requires the frame's `tag` to be `portTag`, so a frame of another
capability, or an untagged one, fails closed; the rest decodes as `inboundBody`.
